Q: What's the best way to handle a callback (wiith named type) that might be unsafe if misused? A:

You are overthinking this a lot. Consider the standard Borrow trait. It is used in HashMap::get method with the following constraint: the borrowed type's Eq and Hash implementations have to be equivalent to the original type's Eq and Hash. There is no way of expressing that in the language itself, and a malicious implementation can break the expected invariant. But then you end up with a broken, completely undefined HashMap.

Not everything can be expressed through the language itself. And you just have to accept that. And create the most basic API you can. And that pretty much always means safe API, with potentially unsafe implementation.

Q: Is spring boot going to be outdated and its developers will going to be laid off? A:

Java and Spring Boot are still pretty much the de facto standard when it comes to enterprise software. I can't see Java going anywhere and because that's a fact, I cannot see Spring Boot going anywhere either. So short-term: you're safe. Long-term: who knows...

Q: Scatterplot with too many points A:

We can also use contour() from base R, i.e., {graphics} with MASS::kde2d() for bivariate kernel density estimation. Extending on what is written here gives

set.seed(1)
X = data.frame(x = rnorm(5000), y = rnorm(5000))
z = MASS::kde2d(X$x, X$y, n = 100)
plot(y~x, data=X, pch = "+", col = "#00000033") # "+" is faster
contour(z, lwd = 2, add = TRUE, 
        col = hcl.colors(10, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE), labels = FALSE)
contour(z, lwd = 0, add = TRUE, col = "black", labcex = 1.1) # labels in black
